terra.problem: The verse does not say he asks for understanding before anything else.
The verse says his hope is in God's word; it does not say his hope is not in a person or a plan.
Saying he is smiling adds an expression the text does not give.
The text does not say he is speaking out loud or whether he is tucking the law away.
His saying that God made him does not mean he could not ask why God made him. That conclusion does not follow from the text.
The wineskin comparison does not say what he looks like. The explanation presents a guessed appearance as fact.
The psalmist says he is like a dried wineskin; the explanation drops the comparison and states that he is dried up. It also states that he feels worn out without marking it as a guess.
Without cause means the persecution is unjustified; it does not establish that the persecutors have no reason or motive at all.
In 'he did not forsake them,' 'them' can refer to the persecutors rather than God's precepts. The explanation needs to make the distinction clear.
The unbaked-cookie line makes the answer choice itself the subject of a joke.
The text does not say the psalmist looks up, or that everything else shakes.
Fixed in the heavens does not establish that the word is in plain view or the opposite of hidden.
The verse says God established the earth and it endures; it does not explicitly say it endures because He established it.
The verse calls all things God's servants. It does not say that being a servant is the opposite of being an enemy.
The explanation is generic and simply repeats that servants serve, without Papa Dorin's distinctive voice.
The claim that the psalmist does not say it lightly assigns him a tone the text does not specify.
Saying he asks for rescue because he belongs to God makes the connection a stated reason. The verse gives his seeking God's precepts as the reason.
The verse says he has seen a limit to all perfection, not that everything else has a limit.
Saying he has seen limits everywhere else goes beyond his statement that he has seen a limit to all perfection.
